  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Planning Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are committed to
the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter and spirit of
Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private life. We
will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest.
We will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of
morality and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We
shall refrain from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and
equitable in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions
in which we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest,
or create a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to
any other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or
censure of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

CHAIR TAPIA  Chair Tapia asked if there are other agencies besides California

  Vehicle Miles Travelled (VMT) is part of CEQA’s transportation

  Responding to a question by Chair Tapia, Assistant Engineer Co
  explained that VMT covers all modes of vehicle traffic. He also added
  that Fehr & Peers were contracted by the City to update any policies or
  guidelines to comply with the State and CEQA regulations.

  Chair Tapia asked for further clarification about CEQA and VMT.
  Assistant City Attorney Guerra explained what CEQA and VMT entails

CHICO  Attorney Guerra stated that the Planning Commission and the City
  Council are the lead agencies for the City. The lead agency will

  the findings to the Planning Commission and if necessary, City Council
  for approval.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Burrola asked for further clarification as to why changes
BURROLA  were made. Assistant Engineer Co stated that Senate Bill 743 was
  passed that resulted in changes to CEQA analysis for transportation..

  changed and what updates have been made to CEQA. Assistant
  Engineer Co clarified that the transportation code has not been
  changed, traffic impact continues to be part of CEQA and is only

  agencies will change the method used to analyze traffic impacts.

Staff Recommendation: That the Planning Commission adopts Resolution No. 783(20)
approving Zone Variance No. 01-2020, finding the projects exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and, subject to the attendant Conditions of Approval.

REQUEST
The applicant is requesting a Zone Variance to exceed the maximum allowable height of
walls, fences or hedges within the required front yard setback.

BACKGROUND/HISTORY
The subject property was developed by the City of Irwindale Housing Authority and IMD
Enterprises, LLC as a single-family housing unit under the comprehensive development
known as “Mayan Housing Project Phases III and IV.” On December 18, 2019, the Planning
Commission unanimously approved Zone Variance No. 02-2019 and 03-2019, allowing a
wrought-iron motorized fence fronting Irwindale Avenue to exceed the maximum height of 3’-
0” due to safety concerns. Shortly after, a 4’-0” motorized gate was installed on the properties
5134 and 5138 Irwindale Avenue. On February 26, 2020, City Council further expressed
safety concerns for the single family homes on Irwindale Avenue and requested consideration
of fencing to be added to the subject property.

GENERAL PLAN AND ZONING
The site is designated in the General Plan as Residential. The site is currently zoned C-3
(Heavy Commercial Residential). Subsection 17.44.010(B) defers all development
restrictions to Chapter 17.16, R-1 (Single-Family Residential). The following zones and uses
surround the site:

  Direction  Existing Land Use  Zoning District
North  Parking Lot/Commercial  C-3, Heavy Commercial Residential
South  Single-Family Homes  C-3, Heavy Commercial Residential
East  Parking Lot/Commercial  C-2, Heavy Commercial
West  Single-Family Homes  R-2, Light-Multiple Residential

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW
The proposed project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
pursuant to Section 15301 (Class 1; Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines. If action is
taken to approve the project, a Notice of Exemption (NOE) will be filed with the County Clerk.
The NOE is on file at the Community Development Department and available for review by
the public.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The subject property is located at 5130 Irwindale Avenue and is ±7,417 square feet in size,
occupied by a ±1,596 square foot single family home.

The location of the subject property is on Irwindale Avenue, one of the collector thoroughfare
of the City. The property is in close proximity to the intersection of Irwindale Avenue and
Arrow Highway, one of the major intersections in the City, which presents life and safety
concerns for the single family residence. The proposed wrought iron fence will exceed the
maximum height limitations in the front yard of the property to provide a buffer between the

Planning Commission Meeting  June 17, 2020

single family home and traffic on Irwindale Avenue. A proposed higher fence would serve as
a safety buffer for future residents of the subject property, and will provide an additional
security barrier against any potential traffic accidents that may occur on Irwindale Avenue. A
higher fence, will also provide additional privacy from pedestrians and vehicle traffic.

A Zone Variance is necessary to allow the maximum height of 3’-0” limitation to be exceeded
for walls, fences or hedges within the required front yard setback.

Zone Variance
When practical difficulties, unnecessary hardships, or results inconsistent with the general
intent and purpose of this title, occur by reason of the strict and literal interpretation of any
of its provisions, a Zone Variance may be granted in the manner set forth per IMC Section
17.80.010. In this case, a Zone Variance is being requested for deviation to exceed the
maximum height limitations within the required front yard setback.

ANALYSIS
Before any Zone Variance is granted, the applicant must show, to the satisfaction of the
Planning Commission or the City Council (if appealed), the existence of the following findings
of fact. Staff has determined that the findings can be made based on the analysis shown:

A.  That there are exceptional or extraordinary circumstances or conditions applicable
  to the property involved or to the intended use of such property, such as size, shape,
  topography location or surroundings, which are not applicable to other properties
  similarly situated.

  The location of the subject property on Irwindale Avenue, near the intersection of
  Irwindale Avenue and Arrow Highway, and adjacent to commercial uses present
  exceptional or extraordinary circumstances in dealing with life and safety concerns
  for the residents of the property. The proposed wrought iron fence, exceeding a
  maximum of a 3’-0” high wall, fence or hedge will enhance the safety and privacy
  against traffic and pedestrians. Additionally, the lot width of the property falls under
  the 60’-0” minimum lot width per the R-1 (Single Family Residential) development
  standards.

B.  That such variance is necessary for the preservation and enjoyment of a substantial
  property right possessed by other property similarly situated, but which is denied to
  the property in question.

  This Zone Variance will enhance the safety and security to the residential use of the
  subject property on Irwindale Avenue, which is a heavily traveled collector street.
  Other residential properties similarly situated within the City possess front yard walls,
  fences or hedges that exceed the maximum height limitations.

C.  That the granting of the variance will not be materially detrimental to the public
  welfare or injurious to the adjacent property.

  The granting of the Zone Variance will not be detrimental to the public welfare or
  injurious to the adjacent properties because the additional height of the fencing is
Planning Commission Meeting  June 17, 2020
Zone Variance No. 01-2020

  solely creating a safety buffer for the private residences and traffic on Irwindale
  Avenue. The residential use of the subject property is also less intense than the
  adjacent commercial uses.

D.  That the granting of the variance will not adversely affect the general intent and
  purpose of this title.

  The granting of the Zone Variance will not adversely affect the general intent and
  purpose of this title. Limitations on wall, fence or hedge height are in place for safety
  and visibility purposes. The applicant’s proposed wrought iron fence will increase the
  maximum allowable height with openings that provide visibility through the fence. As
  such, the proposed fence would not be a hazard for the ingress or egress of vehicles.

CONCLUSION
That the Planning Commission take the following action:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 783(20) approving Zone Variance No. 01-2020, subject to the
  proposed Conditions of Approval to permit the proposed improvements as presented
  herein.

Alternative Actions:

  2. Request that staff prepare resolutions of denial based on recommended Findings of Fact
  to be brought back at the next regularly scheduled Planning Commission meeting for
  adoption; OR

  3. Request that the applicant revise the projects and continue the hearing to a date certain.

  which is denied to the property in question.

  This Zone Variance will enhance the safety and security to the residential use of
  the subject property on Irwindale Avenue, which is a heavily traveled collector
  street. Other residential properties similarly situated within the City possess front
  yard walls, fences or hedges that exceed the maximum height limitations.

C.  That the granting of the variance will not be materially detrimental to the public
  welfare or injurious to the adjacent property.

  The granting of the Zone Variance will not be detrimental to the public welfare or
  injurious to the adjacent properties because the additional height of the fencing is
  solely creating a safety buffer for the private residences and traffic on Irwindale
  Avenue. The residential use of the subject property is also less intense than the
  adjacent commercial uses.
